messages:
kevin: Heads-up — infra repo GH Actions started failing intermittently across matrix runs this morning. Lots of `cache restored` followed by job failures. Example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/12345678 :thinking_face:

infra-bot: Workflow failed: infra-ci (matrix) — job: deploy-helm — exit code 1

maya: Saw a cluster of these around 03:10 UTC. Logs show cache restore succeeded but later steps error with `tar: unexpected EOF` in some jobs and `docker pull` timeouts in others.

kevin: It's flaky — re-running passes. Hypothesis: concurrent cache restores/uploads are colliding (corrupting tar), and separately runner image pulls are timing out on specific self-hosted nodes.

sam: Which cache action are we using? `actions/cache@v3`? In infra CI we key on `terraform-{{ hashFiles('**/*.tf') }}` I think.

kevin: Yes `actions/cache@v3`. Matrix is configured with `concurrency: group: infra-${{ matrix.os }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false`. Might not isolate uploads enough. Also seeing `i/o timeout` on runner cloud-12 during `docker pull`.

liz: We've seen similar when runner nodes are being reprovisioned — in-flight file writes to `/tmp` can corrupt tar archives. Could be preemption or image garbage collection.

maya: Example log snippet: `Cache restored from key: terraform-linux-abc123` then later `tar: unexpected EOF` and elsewhere `error during connect: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": dial tcp: i/o timeout`.

kevin: Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Make cache upload keys include a unique suffix during upload (e.g. run id) to avoid concurrent overwrite.
2) Add backoff/retries for `docker pull` in the job step (3 retries with jitter).
3) Temporarily throttle matrix concurrency (set max 1-2) for infra repo workflows.

sam: +1 on pre-check job to verify runner health before heavy jobs (disk free, DNS, time drift). Could short-circuit fail early.

liz: I'll open a small PR with concurrency change + cache key tweak. Also propose we bump to `actions/cache@v4` and add broader `restore-keys` so partial restores are less brittle.

maya: Also file INFRA ticket to audit runner pool flapping — provider preemptions / node drains might align with timestamps. CC @ops.

ops-bot: Created issue INFRA-4297: "gha infra runner cache corruption & image pull timeouts" — https://tracker.internal/INFRA-4297

kevin: Thanks. I'll hold re-runs of blocked PRs until those changes merge. Anyone object to throttling matrix to 2 instead of 1 for speed tradeoff?

sam: 2 is fine for now.

maya: After merge, monitor for 24h and add alert if `gha_job_retry_count > 3` across infra workflows.

kevin: Good call. Schedule follow-up tomorrow 10:00 PT to review logs.

liz: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/876 — includes: concurrency -> 2, cache key suffix, docker pull retry wrapper.

kevin: I'll merge when green and rerun the failing runs. Quick debug tip: to inspect a suspicious cache tar locally run:
```
# on runner node
tar -tzf /path/to/cache.tgz || echo "tar error"
```

maya: Thanks, will watch alerts. :eyes:
